method.value: Extract a spectrum per pixel, fit emission lines with Gaussians for the Doppler shift; for HC3N and CH3CN fit 3 MHz windows around the line cores with a constant offset; average three CH3CN lines

evidence.quote: This involved extracting individual spectra from the 2016 and 2017 ALMA image cubes and fitting the emission lines with Gaussians to determine their Doppler shifts.
the fits were restricted to narrow (3 MHz wide) spectral regions, centered on each of the line cores.

assumptions.value: Limb emission optically thin and thermally broadened, so the Gaussian Doppler shift gives the line-of-sight wind

evidence.quote: Since the observed limb emission is predominantly optically thin, and originates from sufficiently high altitudes that thermal broadening dominates the line core shapes

The $\pm68^{th}$ percentiles of the resulting parameter distributions are interpreted as $1\sigma$ errors.

findings_qualitative.value: Wind variability grows with altitude: stronger temporal change from CH3CN to HC3N to HNC

evidence.quote: Thus, we see a significant trend for stronger temporal variability with increasing altitude above Titan’s stratosphere.

evidence.quote: the lower-altitude zonal winds revealed by CH$_3$CN reach a peak velocity $11^{\circ}$–$13^{\circ}$ south of the equator (at both epochs)

claims.hypothesis: Titan's thermospheric equatorial jet is temporally variable
claims.experiment: Doppler maps and Gaussian wind-profile fits for CH3CN, HC3N and HNC in August 2016 (reanalysed) and May 2017
claims.result: Peak deconvolved zonal wind speed dropped 27%, 34% and 47% for CH3CN, HC3N and HNC
claims.finding: A large, altitude-dependent slowing of the equatorial jet occurred over 9 months

evidence.quote: a 47% reduction in the equatorial zonal wind speed was measured over the 9-month period (corresponding to $L_s=82^{\circ}$–$90^{\circ}$ on Titan)
A larger drop was observed for HC$_3$N ($34\pm1$%) and larger-still for HNC ($47\pm1$%).

claims.hypothesis: The jet's latitudinal shape changed along with its speed
claims.experiment: Compare fitted Gaussian FWHM and latitudinal offset between epochs
claims.result: HNC FWHM went from 70 to 101 degrees; CH3CN and HC3N shapes unchanged
claims.finding: The thermospheric (HNC) jet lost latitudinal confinement

evidence.quote: the HNC wind profile was subject to substantial broadening, in addition to its dramatic slowing.

claims.hypothesis: The 2016 HNC jet was dynamically unstable
claims.experiment: Rayleigh-Kuo criterion applied to the fitted HNC latitudinal wind profile
claims.result: beta - Uyy << 0 for the 2016 profile, still < 0 at high latitudes in 2017
claims.finding: Dynamical instability explains the slowing and broadening

evidence.quote: The Rayleigh-Kuo criterion shows strong evidence for instability ($\beta-U_{yy}\ll0$) of the HNC thermospheric jet in 2016, as a result of its high speed and narrow FWHM.

claims.hypothesis: Gravity-wave forcing from the middle atmosphere drives the thermospheric jet
claims.experiment: Qualitative comparison with Cassini CIRS and circulation results from other work
claims.result: Reduced middle-atmosphere wind shear in 2016-2017 coincides with the slower jet
claims.finding: Loss of gravity-wave forcing may have slowed the jet; the cause is speculative

evidence.quote: We speculate that the strong, dynamically-unstable thermospheric jet seen by ALMA in 2016 could have been driven by gravity waves

why_this_data.value: Re-analyse the 2016 archive data with the same pipeline as 2017 for consistency

evidence.quote: To ensure consistency of the data analysis methodology between 2016 and 2017, we re-analyzed the CH$_3$CN, HC$_3$N and HNC data observed by (cite: lel19) on 2016-08-18.

why_this_method.value: A Gaussian v(latitude) profile reproduces the main features with few free parameters

evidence.quote: we decided on a Gaussian parameterization, which is able to reproduce the main features in our observed velocity maps, with a minimum number of free parameters

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: 2016 HC3N J=40-39 data rejected for low spectral resolution; J=39-38 used instead

evidence.quote: but at a lower spectral resolution ($\Delta{\nu}=977$ kHz, insufficient for accurate radial velocity measurements), so we instead used observations of the HC$_3$N ($J=39-38$) line

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: More complex latitudinal/longitudinal wind forms considered but not used

evidence.quote: Although more complex functional forms can be envisaged (allowing for longitudinal as well as additional latitudinal variability)

limitations_admitted.value: Wind-field map fidelity limited by coarse altitude sampling and altitude smearing

evidence.quote: The fidelity of these maps is limited by (1) the coarse altitude sampling of our data, (2) smearing due to the broad range of altitudes

limitations_admitted.value: Timescale of the jet variability unknown due to sparse temporal sampling

evidence.quote: Due to the incomplete temporal sampling, however, the actual timescale of the thermospheric jet’s variability remains unknown.

limitations_admitted.value: Retrieved profiles may be biased by emission from altitudes other than the mean contribution altitude

evidence.quote: the possibility that the retrieved velocity profiles could be biased by emission from altitudes different from the mean wind contribution function altitude should be considered

referee_caveats_inferred: Only two epochs, so seasonal versus intermittent variability cannot be separated
Instability conclusion rests on a 1D Gaussian fit with a single altitude per molecule; no formal test of the criterion's sensitivity to fit uncertainty
Flux calibration and absolute velocity systematics beyond rest-frequency errors are not discussed
The 2016 and 2017 data differ in spectral resolution and line sets (HC3N J=39-38 vs 40-39)
